# PDF regression corpus

Seventeen fixtures covering the categories the Milestone 1 spike had to answer
for (PRODUCT_SPEC §22). They are a permanent regression corpus, not throwaway
spike material: later milestones are expected to keep running against them.

## Provenance and licence

Every fixture is **generated by this repository** from prose written for this
repository, by `scripts/generate-pdf-fixtures.mjs`:

```
node scripts/generate-pdf-fixtures.mjs
```

No third-party document, sample PDF or copyrighted text is redistributed here,
which is why the corpus can be committed without a licensing question. The
generator pins creation and modification dates, so regenerating produces
byte-identical files.

Three external inputs are involved in generation:

| Input                          | Role                                                            | Licence                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pdf-lib` + `@pdf-lib/fontkit` | build the documents (dev dependency)                             | MIT                                                                       |
| DejaVu Serif (system font)     | embedded, subset, in `g`, `h`, `k`, `l` for non-ASCII glyphs     | Bitstream Vera licence — free to use, embed, modify and redistribute      |
| `qpdf` (system tool)           | applies AES-256 encryption to `o-encrypted.pdf`                  | Apache-2.0 (tool only; nothing from qpdf is redistributed)                |

The DejaVu subset embedded in four fixtures is the only third-party content in
the committed files. The Bitstream Vera licence explicitly permits embedding
and redistribution. The other fixtures use the PDF standard 14 fonts, which are
font *references*, not embedded data.

Regenerating requires a Linux host with `fonts-dejavu-core` and `qpdf`
installed. On a machine without them the generator fails loudly rather than
silently producing a different corpus.

test fixture; the password is intentionally public.

`p-corrupt.pdf` is deliberately malformed and will be reported as unreadable by
any conforming tool. That is its purpose.

## How they are used

- `tests/integration/*.test.ts` run the real PDF.js engine against every
  fixture under Node (`npm run test:integration`).
- The manual verification recorded in `docs/PDF_SPIKE_REPORT.md` opens the same
  files in the built application.

## M7.5 Slice B extension

The following fixtures were added using `scripts/generate-pdf-fixtures.mjs` with
`M75_OUTPUT_DIR` pointing to a temporary output directory. The generator accepts
these environment variables without changing the default output location:

```text
M75_CJK_FONT   CJK font path; default /usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto/NotoSansCJKjp-Regular.otf
M75_UNICODE_FONT Unicode font path; default /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf
M75_QPDF       qpdf executable; default qpdf on PATH
```

The CJK font used for the committed fixture is the official Noto CJK
`NotoSansCJKjp-Regular.otf`, from the Noto source repository:
`https://github.com/notofonts/noto`. Its SHA-256 is
`68a3fc98800b2a27b371f2fb79991daf3633bd89309d4ffaa6946fd587f375b5`.
The exact upstream release/revision of this installed font was not retained
when the fixture was provisioned and is therefore not claimed here. It is
licensed under the SIL Open Font License, version 1.1; the license text and
terms are available at `https://scripts.sil.org/OFL` and require retaining the
copyright and license notices. Attribution is to the Noto Project, Google Inc.
and the Noto contributors.

The Unicode fixture uses the exact installed file
`/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf`, SHA-256
`57f73e11f51999432bf7ab22ce55b6f945d5eca1bf824404cfa9ec2e3718c84e`, font
version `155320` (DejaVu Sans), from Debian package `fonts-dejavu-core`
version `2.37-8`. DejaVu is based on the Bitstream Vera fonts and is licensed
under the Bitstream Vera and DejaVu license terms. The applicable license and

`https://dejavu-fonts.github.io/License.html`; redistribution must retain

`/usr/share/doc/fonts-dejavu-core/copyright`.

## Observed RTL extraction

The source strings passed to `drawText` are:

```text
שלום
مرحبا
```

The observed PDF.js extraction is:

```text
םולש
ابحرم
```

The fixture verifies glyph coverage, Unicode mappings and character
preservation. It does **not** establish logical reading-order correctness,
Arabic shaping or visual RTL layout. Real selection and lookup behavior remain
for the Electron verification slice. The reversed sequences are recorded as
observed behavior requiring further application-level assessment, not as a
confirmed product defect.


qpdf is an external tool and is not a project dependency. The generator
requires exactly qpdf `12.4.2`; it rejects missing or incompatible versions
before creating the output directory or writing fixtures.

| Fixture | Category and purpose | Bytes | SHA-256 | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `r-cjk-mixed.pdf` | Horizontal Japanese, Chinese and mixed Latin/CJK | 58,248 | `8499268692e4683ae92ec4849a1d03522d96225195b3c79a17f3e38887fc9b9f` | PDF.js extracts `日本語の文章 中文测试 Mixed Latin and CJK.` without replacement characters |
| `s-unicode-representative.pdf` | Combining mark, Hebrew, Arabic and astral-plane character | 8,704 | `f76f4fd80cdc311c1c6a1197e3596d9abfe0e4f4d655c60bb75a1657b8854f` | PDF.js preserves the tested code-point sequences; logical RTL order is recorded by the test |
| `t-owner-password-only.pdf` | Empty user password, non-empty owner password, AES-256, restricted permissions | 2,459 | `350bb538c72f9eb1b9458ca15b42b7bfae7f56d78bc5279dfe066265f7368457` | Opens without a password; PDF.js `getPermissions()` returns `Set(1) { 512 }` |
| `u-invalid-xref-recovery.pdf` | Existing valid fixture with deterministic invalid `startxref` offset | 1,934 | `c4372e2b2b176438a5c78fe89c66140d2a722fe86b10294af0cc68a8d00622cc` | PDF.js and the production adapter recover one page with stable text |

The qpdf-encrypted fixture is not expected to be byte-identical across
regenerations because AES encryption uses randomized file keys. Its encryption
parameters, permission integer and semantic PDF.js behavior are the
reproducibility contract; the fixture checksum above identifies the committed
artifact. The other three fixture outputs matched byte-for-byte in a second
temporary generation.
